LESSON: PUTTING

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.8: Putting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Putting. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Which objects look together learner should be able to: similar objects within their alike?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sets of similar objects together with a sum not objects in the environment exceeding 9 and count. for counting • Two

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Putting.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Putting using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Two learners demonstrate putting c) put similar objects together similar objects together with a sum with a sum not exceeding 9 not exceeding 9 and count. d) enjoy the activities of putting
2. In small groups learners put objects together objects in their day together with a sum not exceeding 9 to day experiences and count. e) appreciate that things become
3. Learners sing songs related to putting more when put together together with sums not exceeding 9 e.g. 1 little brown bird sitting on a wall along came another one and that made two. 63
4. Count and put together objects to get sums of not more than nine (9) using ICT devices.
5. Collaboration and communication as learners join parts to form a whole

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Putting is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
